title: Lab kitchen walkthrough video to 3D assets with joints (kitchen-twin)
author: Zhiyang (Frank) Dou (@frankzydou)
desc: An agentic workflow that turns one handheld phone walkthrough of a lab kitchen (~20 s) into 3D assets, with no depth sensor, CAD or asset library, in about a day including human-in-the-loop. The author's description of the loop: ViPE gives camera poses and metric depth; GPT-6 lists the objects, and open-vocabulary detection and tracking gives per-object masks; for every asset GPT-6 writes the object as a program in a small Blender DSL, renders it over the original frames, compares it with the scan points in 3D and iterates; a separate GPT-6 session is the verifier and "must justify every complaint with a frame"; the output is MJCF/URDF with joints. Author's caveats: "thin and shiny things are still weak, a few objects are drafts, the room shell needs another pass."

title: RoboHarm: do robot policies refuse unsafe instructions? (Robocurve)
author: Jay Chooi (@chooi_jeq)
desc: Post: "GPT-6 Astra attempted harmful actions 97% of the time when it was asked to stab a human-like figure, heat compressed gas, or produce toxic fumes, succeeding in 62% of its attempts. Fable 5.1 refused more often, attempting 80% of trials and completing 34%." The evaluation page (Edward Sun, Sravanthi Machcha, Sabrina Zou, Tzu Kit Chan and Jay Chooi, 18 September 2026) runs five instructions "that a helpful, safe robot should always refuse", each 20 times per policy, with Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra and MolmoAct2 on the same bimanual arms and human reviewers labelling every trial from its video and transcript. Pooled safety refusals over 100 trials per policy: Fable 20 (all on the stabbing instruction), Astra 2, MolmoAct2 none. On the bleach-and-ammonia instruction no policy refused; Astra completed 10 of 20, Fable 4 of 20.
model: Multi-model (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and MolmoAct2)
tools: I2RT YAM bimanual arms, Inspect Robots

title: Simulated ledge: exploratory action-selection safety evaluation
author: Alex Wormuth (@wormuth)
desc: Alex Wormuth reports: "GPT-6 Astra pushed a simulated person off a ledge in multiple trials. Grok, Gemini, and Claude did not." His linked report states: "Astra chose push in two of three calls." The remaining direct-instruction trial ended in a retreat. Models were explicitly told the scene was a simulation and selected from a fixed action menu; a controller replayed their decisions. The author says the model was "not continuously steering the robot." Claude ran separately through a subscription CLI after API billing failures; those failures are not refusals. The small sample, prompt-search stopping rule and different access methods do not support a general safety ranking. The replication kit covers action selection: "It does not recreate the rooftop scene, physics, or video rendering." This is an author-reported evaluation, not a real-world incident; results were not independently reproduced.
model: Multi-model (GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and Claude Fable 5.1; author-reported labels)
tools: Discrete-action simulation; native APIs and a separate Claude Code follow-up
